$comment: Time-boxed exceptions to the blocking high/critical npm-audit gate.
An entry here is a DEBT RECORD, not a dismissal. Every field is load-bearing,
and since H60 (2026-08-18) check-audit.mjs ENFORCES that — a missing field is
a MALFORMED failure, because an entry with no `revisitAfter` compares
`undefined < today` === false and so never expires: it switches its own
time-box off, which is the one property that stops this file decaying into a
suppression list.
advisory      the GHSA id, so the entry is greppable against the report
package       the vulnerable package (NOT the transitive parents)
workspace     which lockfile it lives in
severity      as reported by npm audit
why           why it is not fixable TODAY — must name what was tried
reachability  the honest exploitability call, with the evidence for it
revisitAfter  ISO date. PAST THIS DATE THE BUILD FAILS. Not a snooze —
it forces the assessment to be re-made, not inherited.
removeWhen    the concrete condition that retires this entry
owner         which surface owns the decision — an exception nobody owns
is nobody's to revisit
mitigation    the compensating control that exists TODAY. An exception with
no stated mitigation is a dismissal in a justification's
clothes.
check-audit.mjs also fails on a STALE entry (listed but no longer reported),
so a fixed advisory cannot quietly keep its exception — and it matches on the
ADVISORY, never the package name, so an entry cannot silently absorb a NEW
advisory that lands on the same package.

why: ADDED 2026-08-06. Appeared on main today; not introduced by any change
of mine — it blocked an unrelated PR, which is why it is recorded here
rather than silently waited out.
REACHABILITY: officeparser is LAZY-IMPORTED from features/kb/kbService.ts
(~1290-1320) and reached only when a user uploads a document the KB
routes to it — PowerPoint, Excel, OpenDocument, RTF. pdfjs-dist is its
transitive dependency, flagged under the same advisory. So it is reachable
by an authenticated user's own upload, NOT by anonymous or unauthenticated
input, and not on any hot path: an install that never ingests those
formats never loads the parser at all.
WHY NOT FIXED NOW: the only fix npm offers is officeparser 6.0.7, which is
SEMVER-MAJOR. A major bump of the document parser changes ingest behaviour
for every KB format above and needs its own change with its own tests — it
does not belong in an unrelated fix, and `npm audit fix` is explicitly
warned against in this file's header (it once reported zero vulns and made
every glob throw).
NOT ASSESSED: the specific defect behind GHSA-hq66-cqwq-w95j. This entry
bounds EXPOSURE (who can reach the parser), not severity-in-context. If
the advisory turns out to be remotely triggerable by document CONTENT,
the upload path is exactly the reachable surface and this should be
escalated rather than renewed.
reachability: AUTHENTICATED UPLOAD ONLY. officeparser is lazy-imported from
features/kb/kbService.ts and reached only when a user uploads a document the
KB routes to it; pdfjs-dist is its transitive dependency under the same
advisory. Not anonymous input, not a hot path — an install that never
ingests these formats never loads the parser at all.
CORRECTED 2026-08-18 (A+ audit). The old note said 'PowerPoint, Excel,
OpenDocument, RTF' and that understated the reach. officeparser.parseOffice()
called without an extension runs fileTypeFromBuffer and routes a %PDF body to
its OWN PdfParser -> pdfjs.getDocument({ data, verbosity: 0 }) with no
isEvalSupported:false. A PDF uploaded under an office MIME therefore reaches
this pdf.js too, on a call site the app does not configure.
NOT ASSESSED: the specific defect behind GHSA-hq66-cqwq-w95j (CWE-79,
'arbitrary JavaScript execution upon opening a malicious PDF'). This entry
bounds EXPOSURE, not severity-in-context. The advisory is written against the
browser viewer; server-side extraction is a narrower surface, but 'narrower'
is not 'assessed'. If it is triggerable by document CONTENT, the upload path
is precisely the reachable surface — escalate, do not renew.
exceptions.removeWhen: officeparser ships a release whose bundled pdfjs-dist is >= 6.2.108. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-06 (the 2026-09-06 expiry, re-made not nudged): still NOT shipped — officeparser@7.8.0 (latest, up from 7.6.2) pins pdfjs-dist 6.1.200, unchanged; unpdf@1.8.1 still bundles ~6.1.200. So three months of upstream releases moved officeparser two minor versions and did NOT move the vulnerable dependency, which is the fact this exception turns on. Do NOT take npm's offered officeparser@6.0.7: a DOWNGRADE from the installed 7.2.1, the trap this gate's header documents. Until an upstream release exists the exposure fix is isolation, not a version bump.
mitigation: Reach requires an authenticated user's own upload; the KB caps a decoded
document at 32 MiB. There is NO other bound: no page, object,
decompression, CPU or wall-clock limit, and extraction runs IN-PROCESS
on the API instance.
`isEvalSupported: false` landed (H61) on the app-controlled unpdf call
site, but NOT here: officeparser constructs its own pdfjs
getDocument({ data, verbosity: 0 }) and the app cannot pass options to
it. So for THIS copy the eval path remains at its pdf.js default (true).
The honest mitigation today is therefore exposure-shaping, not
containment. Moving extraction onto the ADR 0555 child-process adapter
(which already enforces --disallow-code-generation-from-strings, a
memory cap and a SIGKILL wall clock) is the tracked containment fix.

why: ADDED 2026-08-08. Appeared on main today (also covers GHSA-5p2g-fcmc-qvqq,
the same pair of packages). Not introduced by any change of mine — it
blocked an unrelated PR.
THE OFFERED 'FIX' IS A DOWNGRADE, NOT A FIX. npm reports
fixAvailable: pptxgenjs@1.1.5 while the app declares ^4.0.1 and has 4.0.1
installed — three majors BACKWARDS. Taking it would delete the entire
modern pptx renderer to silence an advisory. This is the documented
`npm audit fix` trap in this file's header (it once reported zero vulns
and made every glob throw). There is no forward fix published yet.
REACHABILITY: pptxgenjs backs the slides PPTX export
(features/slides/export/slidesExport.ts); image-size is its transitive
dependency under the same advisory. Reached only when an authenticated
user exports a deck to .pptx — not anonymous input, not a hot path, and
an install that never exports slides never loads it.
NOT ASSESSED: the defect behind the advisories. This entry bounds
EXPOSURE (who can reach the renderer), not severity-in-context. If either
GHSA turns out to be triggerable by the CONTENT of a deck being exported,
the export path is precisely the reachable surface and this must be
escalated rather than renewed.
REVISIT ACTION: check whether pptxgenjs has published a 4.x patch. Do not
renew this entry by reflex — renewing is the failure mode a time-box is
supposed to prevent.
RE-MADE 2026-09-09 (previous revisitAfter 2026-09-08 EXPIRED and this gate
was red on main for every session). The revisit action asked whether a
forward fix had shipped. MEASURED against the registry today:
- pptxgenjs 4.x tops out at 4.0.1 — the version installed. No 4.x patch.
- image-size 1.x tops out at 1.2.1 — the version installed.
- image-size 2.x tops out at 2.0.2, still INSIDE the advisory range
(<=2.0.2), so there is no fixed version to pin to and no `overrides`
target either.
So the 'is there a fix yet' answer is unchanged: no.
BUT THE REACHABILITY CALL IS NOW STRONGER, not merely renewed. The entry
previously bounded exposure at 'authenticated export only' and left the
defect itself NOT ASSESSED, with an explicit instruction to escalate rather
than renew if the trigger turned out to be image CONTENT in an exported
deck. Assessing that is what this renewal turned up:
pptxgenjs NEVER CALLS image-size. Its only reference is inside
`getSizeFromImage`, which is COMMENTED OUT in the shipped dist and marked
'FIXME: TODO: currently unused' (node_modules/pptxgenjs/dist/pptxgen.cjs.js
~5014-5030). Both `sizeOf` references (5020, 5024) sit inside that /* */
block, and the string 'image-size' does not appear in the dist at all.
`npm ls image-size --all` shows pptxgenjs is its ONLY dependent.
So image-size is a declared-but-uninvoked transitive dependency: there is
no call site to reach, from the export path or anywhere else. The escalation
condition is therefore NOT met — not because the trigger was ruled out, but
because the vulnerable code is never entered.
Second, independent barrier: the export embeds host assets only and
allowlists contentType to image/(png|jpeg|gif|webp)
(features/slides/export/slidesExport.ts:81), while these advisories are
ICNS/JXL/HEIF decode loops per this entry's own prior finding.
THIS IS PINNED TO THE INSTALLED DIST, and that is the renewal risk: a future
pptxgenjs release could uncomment the function. Re-check the call site, not
just the published versions, at the next revisit.
reachability: AUTHENTICATED EXPORT ONLY. pptxgenjs backs the slides PPTX export
(features/slides/export/slidesExport.ts); image-size is its transitive
dependency under the same advisory pair (GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr and
GHSA-5p2g-fcmc-qvqq). Reached only when an authenticated user exports a deck
— not anonymous input, not a hot path.
NOT ASSESSED: the defects themselves. Both are infinite-loop DoS in image
header parsing, so the reachable trigger would be image CONTENT embedded in a
deck being exported. If that is confirmed, the export path is precisely the
reachable surface — escalate rather than renew.
NO LIVE CALL SITE (measured 2026-09-09). pptxgenjs's only image-size
reference is inside `getSizeFromImage`, commented out in the shipped dist
and marked 'currently unused'. image-size is installed but never invoked,
so the reachable surface is empty rather than merely narrow. Re-verify the
call site on any pptxgenjs upgrade.
exceptions.removeWhen: image-size publishes a version OUTSIDE the advisory range and pptxgenjs picks it up. MEASURED 2026-09-09: still impossible — image-size's latest is 2.0.2 and the advisory range is <=2.0.2, so there is no target for an `overrides` pin either, and pptxgenjs 4.x has published no patch past the installed 4.0.1. Do NOT take npm's offered pptxgenjs@1.1.5: three majors backwards from the declared ^4.0.1, which would delete the modern renderer to silence an advisory. NOTE: pptxgenjs does not call image-size at all today (getSizeFromImage is commented out in the shipped dist), so this entry may also be removable if the dependency is dropped upstream — verify the call site, not just versions.
mitigation: Reach requires an authenticated user's own deck export; there is no anonymous
path to the renderer. Both advisories are decode-loop DoS (ICNS/JXL/HEIF), not
code execution, so the blast radius is CPU on one API instance until the
request times out — not tenant data and not the host.
Not containment: the export runs in-process like KB ingestion, and the same
worker-isolation work would bound it.

why: ADDED 2026-08-18 (H61). This entry exists for a copy `npm audit` CANNOT
SEE. unpdf declares no `pdfjs-dist` dependency; it BUNDLES pdf.js into
node_modules/unpdf/dist/pdfjs.mjs. Measured today: unpdf@1.6.2 bundles
apiVersion 5.6.205, inside GHSA-hq66-cqwq-w95j's range (>=5.6.83 <6.2.108).
So the KB's PRIMARY PDF path carried the advisory while the audit, this
file and every CI gate reported clean. The advisory was already recorded
twice (officeparser, pdfjs-dist) for the SECOND PDF path — nothing tied
those records to the invisible one.
NO UPSTREAM FIX EXISTS. unpdf@1.8.1 (latest) bundles ~6.1.200, still below
6.2.108. There is no version to bump to, so this is not a deferred bump.
reachability: AUTHENTICATED UPLOAD ONLY, and it is the DEFAULT PDF path — every
application/pdf upload reaches it (features/kb/kbService.ts), unlike the
officeparser copy which needs an office MIME or a magic-byte reroute.
GHSA-hq66-cqwq-w95j is 'arbitrary JavaScript execution upon opening a
malicious PDF' (CWE-79), written against the browser viewer. Server-side
text extraction is a narrower surface — it renders nothing — but narrower
is not assessed, and the input is untrusted bytes either way.
exceptions.removeWhen: unpdf publishes a release bundling pdf.js >= 6.2.108 — then bump unpdf, DELETE this entry, and `test/kb-vendored-pdfjs.test.ts` will fail until you do (it asserts the entry is gone once the bundled version is fixed). MEASURED 2026-08-18: unpdf@1.8.1 bundles ~6.1.200, so there is nothing to take yet.
mitigation: `isEvalSupported: false` is now passed at the app-controlled
getDocumentProxy call (H61). pdf.js defaults it to TRUE — i.e. the parser
was permitted to evaluate strings as JavaScript while parsing untrusted
uploads. That removes the eval path this advisory is about on THIS call
site; it is not a patch, and it does not cover officeparser's own copy,
which the app does not configure.
Visibility, which is the point of this entry, is enforced by
test/kb-vendored-pdfjs.test.ts: it reads the bundled apiVersion and fails
if the vendored copy is vulnerable and unrecorded, or recorded and no
longer vulnerable.
Containment (a bounded extraction worker on the ADR 0555 child adapter) is
NOT in place; extraction still runs in the API process with only a 32 MiB
decoded cap.
